title: NY State Assembly · District 62
area: Staten Island's South Shore and parts of Mid-Island

context.text: This is an uncontested race. Democrats did not field a candidate. Incumbent Michael Reilly (R, Conservative) advanced from both the Republican and Conservative primaries scheduled for June 23, 2026, which were canceled, and is the only candidate on the November ballot. A primary challenger, John A. Tabacco, withdrew or was disqualified from the Republican primary.

candidates.name: Michael Reilly
candidates.currentRole: NY State Assembly Member, District 62 (since January 2019); Ranking Minority Member, Assembly Committee on Cities

summary.text: Michael Reilly is the incumbent Republican and Conservative Assembly Member for District 62, running unopposed. A retired NYPD lieutenant and Army Reserve veteran, he is the Ranking Minority Member of the Assembly's Cities Committee.

background.text: Reilly served in the United States Army Reserve before joining the New York City Police Department, where he served 12 years and retired as a Lieutenant from Brooklyn's 90th Precinct.

In 2009 he became a volunteer member of Community Education Council 31, focusing on accountability and transparency at NYC public schools; he served as the Council's president from 2014 until his 2018 election to the Assembly, and became an advocate for traffic safety around school zones.
He previously served as a volunteer member of the Staten Island YMCA's Board of Managers and coached the YMCA's youth baseball league.
He resides in the Eltingville section of Staten Island with his wife and three children.

priorities.text: "Assemblymember Reilly's priorities have been improving our education and transportation systems, ensuring adequate funding for our schools and community programs, combatting the state's devastating opioid crisis, supporting law enforcement officers, and bolstering public safety."

positions.summary: Sponsored a bill barring schools, day cares, and community-based organizations serving children from being used as migrant shelters.

record.text: Serves as Ranking Minority Member of the Assembly Committee on Cities; also a member of the Codes, Education, Governmental Employees, Higher Education, and Housing committees.

Prime sponsor of A10825, which would create a state personal income tax credit of up to $1,000 for tolls paid by New Yorkers commuting on toll roads; referred to the Ways and Means Committee, no floor vote as of September 2026.

Prime sponsor of A04123, which would bar schools, child day cares, day care centers, and community-based organizations serving children under 18 from being used as migrant shelters; referred to committee, no floor vote as of September 2026.

Prime sponsor of A04155, which would allow judicial discretion based on dangerousness for pretrial detention, extend the criminal discovery period from 20 to 45 days, and permit immediate bench warrants for failure to appear on hate-crime charges; referred to the Codes Committee, no floor vote as of September 2026.

Introduced the Toll Payer Advocacy and Relief Act (TPARA), which would bar E-ZPass late fees for the first 180 days after a toll and cap subsequent penalties at 10% of the original toll, following his call for a state investigation into E-ZPass operator Conduent.
